content:
Morgan: Heads up — we need a concrete, ops-ready proposal for request/response logging that covers sampling, PII redaction, and routing-aware quotas for Dedicated/Private customers. Quick sketch below, looking for objections or missing edge cases.

Morgan: Proposal (sketch):
```yaml
log_policy_version: 2
default_sample_rate: 0.01  # 1% global default
region_overrides:
  eu: 0.001  # stricter by default for GDPR
  us: 0.01
per_tenant:
  sampling_mode: consistent_hash
  hash_key: tenant_id
  sample_buckets: 100000
redaction_rules:
  - type: pii_token_mask  # mask "email|ssn|creditcard" by token pattern
  - type: preserve_hash  # keep hashed identifiers for billing & debug mapping
  - type: embeddings_strip_raw  # never store raw embedding inputs; store fingerprint only
retention:
  debug_raw_ttl: 86400  # 24h if customer opts in to debug capture
  default_ttl: 2592000  # 30d for sampled logs
routing_integration:
  route_tiers:
    - name: hosted
      sample_budget_per_minute: 10000
    - name: dedicated
      sample_budget_per_minute: 50000
    - name: private
      sample_budget_per_minute: 20000
  fallback: route_to_hosted_on_overrun: true
```

Morgan: Notes:
- Use consistent-hash sampling keyed on tenant + route so customers get stable samples.
- Do not store raw prompt or raw embedding vectors unless explicit opt-in.
- Quota-aware sampler: sampler should decrement route/tenant sample budget before persisting.

Jamal: Quick q — preserved hashed IDs ok for billing / debug, right? we need deterministic mapping so we can attribute traces back to a tenant without storing PII.

Anya: yes, hashed IDs are fine as long as salt is tenant-scoped and not reversible. Also: never store raw embeddings. Store only a fingerprint (sha256 of input) + vector metadata (dim, quantization). If debug enabled, raw can be kept ephemeral and encrypted.

ops-bot: lint: log_policy_v2.yaml passed schema check (CI #4521) :white_check_mark:

Leo: UX question — how do we expose sampling toggles in the Console? Per-route, per-environment, per-tenant? I worry about accidental high sampling causing big egress costs.

Anya: Per-route with inheritance. Default at org level, override at route. Console should show estimated monthly tokens and budget impact before you save. Also add a reverse-preview showing how many requests would be captured at current traffic profile (:eyes:).

Tia: legal/ops: for EU regulated customers we should default to minimal collection (0.1% or less) and require explicit opt-in for increased debug capture. Also add consent flag so that customer-managed privacy prefs can toggle raw retention.

Morgan: updated sketch: added region_overrides and consent_flag. Also thinking about a runtime switch: if sample_budget exhausted, sampler should: 1) stop sampling 2) mark route as throttled in console and 3) optionally fallback to lower-fidelity capture (headers+metrics only, no payload). Thoughts?

Jamal: Agree. For fairness we should use per-tenant bucket allocation derived from committed capacity (dedicated customers get higher budget). Also propose a token-cost estimator so route owners can set guardrails.

Anya: +1 to the low-fidelity fallback. Add a rule that embeddings requests always fall back to metadata-only capture first.

Leo: Console bits: we can add a sampling preview panel that runs on historical traffic to estimate capture counts. Low lift to implement as a background job.

Tia: Add audit logs for any time raw capture is enabled for a tenant (who enabled it, when, TTL). Compliance will insist on it.

Morgan: Checklist for next steps:
- (Jamal) design deterministic sampler algorithm + budget accounting (RFC)
- (Anya) finalize redaction rule set + schema for fingerprinting embeddings
- (Leo) mock Console UX for per-route sampling + preview + alerts
- (Tia) legal language for consent & EU defaults
- (Infra) implement budget-exhausted fallback behavior in sampler runtime

Anya: happy to take redaction piece, will draft rules and example regexes.

Jamal: OK I'll start the sampler RFC and include pseudo-code for consistent hash buckets.

Morgan: Awesome. If no blockers I want to prep for an eng sync next Tue to lock this in. :thumbsup:

Leo: :thumbsup:

Tia: :eyes: will review legal text once Anya posts it.
